title: Docker Architecture — Client · Daemon · Registry
subtitle: docker run / build / pull route through dockerd to images, containers, and registries

nodes.label:
Docker CLI
docker run / build / pull / push

Docker Daemon (dockerd)
REST API on UNIX socket
Manages all Docker objects

Images
Read-only layer stack
Built from Dockerfile

Containers
Runnable image instances

panels.title: docker run — what actually happens
panels.body:
1. CLI sends request to daemon via UNIX socket (/var/run/docker.sock)
2. Daemon checks local image cache
3. If image missing → pulls layers from registry
4. Daemon unpacks layers via overlayfs into container rootfs
5. Creates namespaces (PID / net / mount / UTS / IPC)
6. Applies cgroup limits (CPU / memory / pids)
7. Execs the ENTRYPOINT/CMD process as PID 1

panels.title: docker build — layer creation
panels.body:
1. CLI sends Dockerfile + build context (tar) to daemon
2. Each FROM pulls (or reuses cached) base image
3. Each RUN / COPY / ADD creates a new read-only layer
4. Layers are content-addressed (SHA256 of content)
5. Identical layer = cache hit → skip rebuild
6. Final layer stack becomes a new image ID
7. docker push uploads new/changed layers to registry

panels.title: Docker daemon vs Podman (daemonless)
pros: Docker: single daemon = simple socket API, mature BuildKit, Docker Compose, Desktop
Podman: no daemon = no single root SPOF, rootless by default, systemd-friendly
cons: Docker daemon runs as root — compromise = full host access
Podman: some Compose compatibility gaps, less BuildKit feature parity
